key_insight: Re-Search turns research ideation into a Twenty Questions–style game: an LLM asks yes-or-no questions to rediscover a published paper’s core idea. This makes the model’s step-by-step search process visible rather than judging only its final proposal.
problem_solved: Existing evaluations obscure how LLMs explore and refine research ideas, making it difficult to identify what limits their progress.
method: Give a model only the research problem addressed by a published paper.
Let it ask yes-or-no questions to narrow down the paper’s core idea.
Examine the questioning process to study how the model explores and refines candidate ideas.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this framework offers a way to evaluate the process behind AI-generated research ideas, not just the end result. It could help diagnose weaknesses in iterative exploration and feedback use; the provided abstract excerpt does not report empirical findings.
visual_elements: Two-player dialogue diagram showing an LLM asking questions and a responder returning yes/no feedback.
Branching decision tree illustrating how answers narrow the space of possible research ideas.
Step-by-step funnel from research problem to candidate ideas to rediscovered core idea.
Side-by-side comparison of final-output evaluation versus process-visible evaluation.
paper_title: Re-Search: Dissecting LLM Ideation Through a Two-Player Questioning Game
paper_authors: Muhan Gao, Hangxiao Zhu, Xinqi Su, Yu Zhang, Daniel Khashabi
